title: Spec Area (area | contract)
description: One JSON file per area at specs/<name>.area.json (kind area) or specs/<name>.contract.json (kind contract) — the filename suffix encodes the kind and must match it. The formal Quint model lives in a sidecar specs/<name>.qnt referenced from formal_model.quint_file. Two kinds: 'area' (functional, default — may carry UI blocks screens/ui_components/navigation to model an interactive surface) and 'contract' (cross-area agreement, spec-only). Most fields are optional; required fields are gated by kind or block presence. Sections grow conversationally via /spec — empty arrays/objects are valid for incomplete specs.

witnessDelta.description: The PRE-state the witnessing step must start from. A postcondition alone proves reachability, not causation: a guard that already implies its own postcondition makes the action a no-op that only fires once its result already holds, and the probe goes green over dead text. The probe conjoins this over `_prev*` ghosts snapshotted before the step, so the trace must show the state actually MOVING. Referenced from BOTH the witness (a `must` has one) and each permitted outcome (a `may` proves each outcome with its own probe, so each names its own pre-state) — tools/spec-probes.py reads outcomes[].delta, which this schema previously forbade outright.

pre.description: Quint boolean over the `_prev*` ghost vars, true exactly when the pre-state was one this behavior could still change. For a lockout: `_prevAccountStatus.get(_lastUid) == Unlocked`.

kind.description: area: functional area (default) — may carry UI blocks (screens/ui_components/navigation); UI-specific lint, readback, and codegen trigger on block presence, not kind. contract: cross-area invariant carrier, spec-only, requires spans[].

area.description: Slug, also the filename stem: specs/<area>.<kind>.json. Examples: auth, billing, auth-ui, user-permission.

spans.description: Areas this spec depends on. Contracts: the 2+ areas the contract joins (required). Areas with UI blocks: the area(s) whose state the surface reads (e.g. ['auth']).

purpose.description: One paragraph: what this area is responsible for.

brief.description: Authored prose that orients a human before the machine-checked detail. The ONE long-form thing an agent writes into the readback — everything else there is derived from fields. Prose cannot be checked the way a witness can, so it carries a freshness pin instead: `written_against` records the spec sha it was written for, and spec-lint flags it once the spec moves. Rendered verbatim and marked as narrative rather than verified fact, so the readback stays byte-identical for identical input.

text.description: Lead paragraph(s), Markdown. If it needs its own headings it is competing with the generated sections instead of introducing them.

how_it_fits.description: Optional facet: the area's shape — main entities, how they relate, the flow through them. The orientation a new reviewer lacks.

why_this_way.description: Optional facet: the reasoning behind the shape. Complements decisions[], which record what was decided but not the narrative joining them.

watch_out_for.description: Optional facet: the sharp edges — what is easy to get wrong, which requirements interact, where the open questions bite.

written_against.description: sha256 from `tools/itf_tools.py spec-sha <area>` — the semantic spec content this brief was written for. Mismatch means the spec moved and the brief may describe something no longer there.

author.description: Who wrote it. A human-written brief is not re-authored by the agent without asking.

boundary.description: The SUBSTITUTION boundary: what would have to stay identical for a different implementation of this area to be a drop-in replacement. `scope` says what the area is responsible for; this says what 'the same' means. Without it, 'the regenerated code matches' has no referent — and the differential runner has nothing to compare. Most valuable on brownfield areas, where an implementation already exists and can serve as the oracle.

entry_points.description: The callable surface clients depend on, with argument shape: 'login(email, password)'. A replacement must accept these.

observable_state.description: What a client can read back and therefore can notice changing. These are what the differential comparator diffs after each step — typically the same abstractions the conformance adapter's getters expose.

persistence_contract.description: Whether the stored representation is part of the contract, and how much of it. The one people forget: behavior can match perfectly while a regenerated schema orphans every existing row. State it explicitly, including 'none — the store is private and may be replaced'.

emits.description: Outward signals other systems consume — events, webhooks, audit records. Observable whether or not anyone calls them API.

free.description: Deliberately NOT preserved: file layout, log wording, internal structure, algorithmic approach. Naming these is what keeps the spec a specification rather than a transliteration — a spec that pins everything can no longer disagree with the code, so it inherits its bugs as truth.

scope.description: The declared semantic boundary. Completeness is only meaningful relative to a boundary: without one, 'closed' is an unbounded claim nobody can check, and every OUT-OF-SCOPE triage verdict is an unfalsifiable assertion. Declaring it turns both into checkable statements — the readback's ship verdict reads 'READY relative to this scope', and spec-lint requires an OUT-OF-SCOPE cell to name the exclusion that covers it.

included.description: Capabilities this area is answerable for, in domain words (cart, checkout, payment authorization).

excluded.description: Capabilities deliberately NOT covered. Each needs a reason: an exclusion without one is indistinguishable from an oversight.

reason.description: Why it is out: owned by another area, deferred, or genuinely not this product's job.

owner.description: The area or team that owns it instead, when there is one.

concepts.description: Vocabulary: entities, actors, verbs. The 'what we're talking about' layer that informs the formal model.

closed.description: CLOSED WORLD: states[] is exhaustive — no other externally meaningful state exists, and no other may be invented downstream. spec-lint then requires the sidecar's variant type to have exactly these constructors (no more, no fewer), so an LLM adding a state to the model, or code adding one to an enum, is caught rather than absorbed. Leave false/absent for a set that is genuinely open to extension.

actors.description: Who/what can initiate actions: User, Admin, System, ScheduledJob, etc.

verbs.description: Domain actions: login, charge, expire, etc. Loose — gets refined into Quint actions during formalization.

externals.description: External systems this area depends on, with the FULL set of outcomes each can produce. Declaring them turns 'what if the payment provider times out?' from a question nobody asked into a matrix cell that must be covered or triaged. An external with no declared outcomes is an idealized dependency — the most common place real-world semantics go missing.

outcomes.description: Every outcome the dependency can produce, INCLUDING the unhappy ones (DECLINED, TIMEOUT, NETWORK_ERROR, DUPLICATE). Each becomes a row in the external×outcome completeness matrix.

terminal.description: True when the outcome ends the interaction (no retry/poll can follow).

assumptions.description: Environment facts the specification RELIES ON but does not establish. First-class because a verification result that depends on an unstated assumption overclaims: the readback annotates every invariant an assumption bears on, so a ✓ reads 'holds, given ASM-001' rather than 'holds'. Never silently treat an external system as ideal — write the idealization down here.

statement.description: The assumed fact, stated so it could in principle be falsified. 'PaymentProvider eventually responds', not 'PaymentProvider is reliable'.

kind.description: 'unrepresentable' is the sharpest case: something the MODEL cannot express and therefore cannot be wrong about — monotonic clocks, atomic increments, single-writer storage, bounded skew. The model is silent on it by construction, so silence must not be mistaken for coverage.

external.description: The externals[].name this assumption is about, when it is about one.

affects.description: IDs whose verification depends on this assumption (INV-NNN, PROP-NNN, REQ-NNN). The single direction of the link — invariants do not list their assumptions, so there is one source of truth. Drives the readback's 'under ASM-NNN' annotation.

status.description: 'accepted': believed and relied upon. 'accepted-risk': known to be possibly false, shipped anyway — requires a `rationale` saying who accepted it and why. 'open': undecided, blocks approval. 'retired': no longer relied upon.

rationale.description: Required for status 'accepted-risk'. An assumption knowingly carried as risk needs its argument recorded, or the next reader cannot tell a considered bet from an oversight.

discharged_by.description: How the assumption is monitored or tested in the real system, if it is (an alert, a contract test). Absent means: believed, not checked.

extraction_triage.description: COMMITTED triage of code sites against the spec — the only check in the framework that runs code → spec rather than spec → code. Every branch, guard literal and error handler in a traced file either maps to a spec element or is explained here. This is where the branches that make a regenerated implementation differ actually live: they are never in the spec, so nothing spec-shaped can look for them.

file.description: Path relative to the code root.

fingerprint.description: Stable hash of the normalized site text, from tools/spec-extract-audit.py. Identity survives the site moving, which a line number does not — a ledger keyed on line numbers rots on the first reformat.

line.description: Advisory only: where the site was last seen.

snippet.description: The site's source text, trimmed. Present so the ledger is reviewable without opening the file.

verdict.description: MAPPED: realizes the spec element in maps_to. NOT-BEHAVIOR: logging, metrics, tracing — real code, no externally observable behavior. DEFENSIVE: unreachable by construction, kept as a belt. DEAD: unreachable, and that is a finding about the CODE. GAP: real behavior nobody has specified — the extraction hole, tracked by a question. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary; cite the exclusion.

maps_to.description: Required for MAPPED: the spec ids this site realizes (REQ/INV/CON/...).

reason.description: Required for every verdict except MAPPED.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item covering it.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

outcome_triage.description: COMMITTED triage for external×outcome cells no requirement handles — the failure-behavior twin of matrix_triage. Same verdicts, same durability rationale: the generated view under specs/<area>/gen/ is gitignored scratch, this is the reviewable home.

verdict.description: GAP: a real hole, tracked by a question. IMPOSSIBLE: the cell cannot occur (a guard forbids it). NO-OP: the event CAN occur here and deliberately changes nothing — the third answer a closed specification needs, and the one most often left implicit; name the requirement that decided it in `reason`. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary, and must cite the scope.excluded[] entry that covers it.

reason.description: Why: the impossibility argument, the covering artifact, or (for GAP) the unanswered question.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item that covers this cell.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

examples.description: Author-written concrete scenarios: given → when → expect. SEEDS AND REGRESSIONS, never the proof — a machine-found witness trace demonstrates that a behavior is reachable, while an example only asserts one case the author had in mind. Their value is brownfield capture (write down what production is known to do before any model exists) and pinning a case a counterexample once broke. Compiled to a Quint `run` and replayed through the same conformance harness as witness traces.

given.description: Starting state as var → value, in the model's own vocabulary. Absent means the initial state.

action.description: Quint action name — must exist in the sidecar.

expect.description: Expected resulting state as var → value.

quint_run.description: Name of the generated `run` in the sidecar, once formalized.

trace.description: For a HARVESTED example: the ITF trace recorded from the real system, relative to specs/. Greenfield examples are guesses about what matters; harvested ones are evidence, and they replay through the same machinery as a witness trace.

id.description: REQ-NNN for functional behavior; UI-NNN for areas with UI blocks; REQ-CONTRACT-NNN for kind=contract.

description.description: Human-readable rendering. When ears is present this is derived from it; the EARS fields are the source of truth.

type.description: non-functional requirements are exempt from witness obligations (no reachable state change to demonstrate) but MUST carry fit_criterion — a measurable acceptance bound. spec-lint enforces.

fit_criterion.description: Measurable acceptance criterion (Planguage-style). Required for type: non-functional — 'fast', 'secure', 'scalable' are not requirements until they carry a metric, a target, and a way to measure. spec-lint WARNs while the requirement is in an early status (raw, needs-validation) and FAILs after.

metric.description: What is measured, with units. E.g. 'p99 login latency (ms)'.

target.description: The bound that must hold. E.g. '< 250ms under 100 rps'.

measurement.description: How/where it is measured. E.g. 'k6 load test in CI, scenario login-storm'.

modality.description: The deontic force, which decides what counts as discharging the requirement. 'must': exactly this outcome is required — one witness trace. 'may': the system is PERMITTED several outcomes and the choice is not the spec's to make — needs a witness per permitted outcome (witness.outcomes[]), so that a nondeterministic allowance is not silently narrowed to whichever branch the implementer picked. 'forbidden': the behavior must never occur — no witness can exist for a non-event, so it must name the invariant that enforces it (witness.enforced_by).
modality.$comment: MAY quietly becoming MUST is one of the specific failure modes this field exists to prevent.

determinism.description: Whether equivalent inputs in equivalent states must produce one observable result. 'deterministic' is a checkable claim; 'nondeterministic' says the latitude is intentional; 'unspecified' says nobody has decided — which is fine early and a gap later. modality 'may' implies nondeterministic.

error_outcomes.description: How this requirement responds to each external outcome it can meet. This is what makes the external×outcome matrix computable: a cell is covered when some requirement names it here. Failure behavior stops being an afterthought precisely when it has to be written down per outcome.

outcome.description: One of that external's declared outcomes[].name.

effect.description: What the system does: 'NO_CHANGE' (transaction rolled back, nothing observable happened), a declared entity state the subject moves to (e.g. 'Pending'), 'RETRY', or 'error:<code>'. Free-form but conventional; the point is that SOMETHING is written for every outcome.

idempotent.description: True when repeating the operation after this outcome is safe — the field that turns 'is a retry harmful?' from tribal knowledge into spec.

extraction.description: Where this item came from when it was read out of existing code. Makes the confirm pass jump-to-site instead of guess-what-I-meant, and lets the extraction audit tell a specified site from an unexamined one.

fingerprint.description: The extraction_triage[] site this item was read from, when it came from exactly one.

confidence.description: low = the code was ambiguous and a human guessed. Worth revisiting before approval; the readback surfaces it.

inferred_by.description: 'agent' | 'human' | 'agent+confirmed'. A confirmed inference is not the same claim as an unreviewed one.

meaning.description: The requirement in plain words — what it MEANS, written by whoever understood what the identifiers and exception names in the EARS fields stand for. 'refuse with NonMatchingTopologyException on serviceLevelPolicyId' names two symbols and asserts nothing a reviewer without the code can agree or disagree with; the meaning says what condition holds and what the system does about it. This is the sentence the readback prints as the requirement's headline; the EARS sentence moves into the collapsed details beside the Quint action, so the names stay one click away. Like a brief, it is prose and cannot be machine-checked, so it carries a freshness pin per requirement: `written_against` records the requirement sha it was written for, and spec-lint flags it once that requirement moves.

text.description: One or two sentences, plain English, no identifiers carrying the load. Declared state, screen and entity names are welcome — those are the vocabulary, not the leakage.

written_against.description: sha256 from `tools/itf_tools.py meaning-sha <area>` — the requirement content this meaning restates. Mismatch means the requirement moved and the plain-words sentence may describe something no longer specified.

author.description: Who wrote it. A human-written meaning is not re-authored by the agent without asking.

ears.description: EARS-structured requirement (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax). The fields ARE the structure — the EARS pattern is derived from which are filled (trigger → 'When …', state → 'While …', both → complex, feature → 'Where …'; none → ubiquitous, which belongs in invariants[] instead). Mapping to Quint: trigger → action, state → require guard, response → effect. spec-lint validates; a requirement without ears past status raw/needs-validation gets a WARN.

state.description: Precondition / system mode ('While ...'). Maps to a Quint require guard.

trigger.description: Initiating event ('When/If ...'). Maps to a Quint action. Required when unwanted is true.

unwanted.description: True when this is error/abnormal-situation handling ('If <trigger>, then …'). The one EARS distinction not derivable from field presence.

response.description: What the system shall do. Maps to the Quint action's effect.

witness.description: Witness obligation: machine-found proof that this behavior is reachable in the model. /spec-check negates the predicate, runs the checker, and saves the counterexample (= the witness trace) as ITF. status 'no-witness' means the behavior is UNREACHABLE — a vacuity red flag. spec-lint blocks approval while any requirement is unwitnessed.

predicate.description: Quint boolean expression (or val name) over state that is true exactly when the required behavior has happened. Example for 'account locks after N failures': accountStatus.keys().exists(u => accountStatus.get(u) == Locked).

trace.description: ITF trace path relative to specs/, e.g. 'auth/traces/REQ-003.itf.json'. Written by /spec-check.

status.description: 'witnessed' = a trace shows the behavior happening. 'no-witness' = UNREACHABLE (impossible guard or missing action). 'hollow' = the predicate was ALREADY TRUE before anything happened: the checker returned a single-state counterexample, so the trace shows the initial state satisfying the predicate, not the behavior occurring. A hollow witness is a false proof and gates exactly like a missing one — the usual fix is a witness.delta forcing the step to move the state, and often a predicate that was too weak to distinguish before from after.

justification.description: Discharges a 'skipped' status when witness.enforced_by is not set; prefer enforced_by, which is checkable. Typical case: a rejection requirement ('shall be rejected') has no state change to witness — pair it with the invariant that stays true and point here, e.g. 'rejection — enforced by INV-002 noSessionWhileLocked'.

enforced_by.description: For modality 'forbidden': the invariant that carries the proof, as an ID rather than prose. Typing the old free-text justification means the link is checkable — spec-lint FAILs a dangling reference instead of trusting a sentence.

outcomes.description: For modality 'may': one entry per PERMITTED outcome, each with its own predicate and its own machine-found trace. A single trace would only prove that one of the allowed behaviors is reachable, which is exactly how a MAY silently degrades into a MUST.

name.description: Short label for this permitted outcome (used to name its probe).

predicate.description: Quint boolean expression true exactly when THIS outcome happened.

trace.description: ITF trace path relative to specs/.

status.description: Same values as witness.status; 'hollow' means this outcome's predicate already held in the initial state.

model_sha.description: sha256 of the model the trace was found against (.qnt + .probes.qnt; see `tools/itf_tools.py sha <area>`). spec-lint FAILs when this no longer matches — a trace from an older model proves nothing about the current one.

refusal.description: Code-side evidence for a REJECTION requirement. Such a requirement produces no state change, so it correctly has no witness trace — and conformance replay only replays witness traces. Without this block the requirement class most likely to be wrong in the implementation carries zero code-side evidence: a login() written with no locked-account check replays every happy-path trace green, passes the tampered self-tests, and /spec-code-verify reports pass.

artifact.description: Path of the test that drives the code into the blocking state, attempts the call, and asserts BOTH that it is refused AND that no observable var moved.

blocking_state.description: The state the code must be driven into first, in the model's vocabulary (e.g. 'accountStatus[uid] == Locked').

unchanged.description: Observable vars that must be identical after the refused call. This half is what makes it a refusal: a rejection that throws AFTER incrementing the counter is not a rejection.

quint_ref.description: Name of the Quint action that realizes this requirement.

over.description: Which module this invariant is checked against. 'model' (default): the area's Quint sidecar with its own init/step, so the invariant can only see one state. 'probes': the generated probe module, run with --init=initP --step=stepP, which puts the `_prev*` ghosts and `_lastAction` in scope. That is the difference between a state property and a TRANSITION property — "a group's policy never changes" is not expressible over a single state, but becomes an ordinary invariant once the pre-state is a variable (`groups.get(g).policy == _prevGroups.get(g).policy`). Without it such requirements have no checkable form and fall back to prose. Requires formal_model.probes_file. Bounded or inductive exactly as on the model path; the module changes, the honesty of the verdict does not.

quint_name.description: Name of the Quint `val` or `invariant` that encodes this.

proof.description: How this invariant is checked. 'bounded' (default): Apalache bounded model check to apalache.max_steps — a ✓ means 'no counterexample within N steps', NOT a proof. 'inductive': Quint runs `--inductive-invariant=<quint_name>` (base case + one-step preservation) — a ✓ means proven across ALL reachable states. 'structural': checked by the Alloy backend over the finite scope declared in the .als command — a ✓ means 'no counterexample within that scope', a different bound from the step bound. 'smt': discharged by an SMT solver over the query in smt_file — no state machine, no trace, just a theory-level fact (arithmetic, data consistency); unsat on the negation means proven modulo the encoding, and 'unknown' is reported as not-checkable rather than as a pass. Render distinguishes all four (✓ proven vs ✓ (≤N steps) vs ✓ (scope: …) vs ✓ (smt)).

alloy_command.description: Required when proof is 'structural': the name of the `check` command in formal_model.alloy_file that encodes this invariant. spec-record runs it via `alloy exec -c <name>` and reads the verdict from receipt.json.

smt_file.description: Required when proof is 'smt': path (relative to specs/) of the SMT-LIB2 query asserting the NEGATION of this invariant. `unsat` = no violating assignment exists = the invariant holds; `sat` = the model is a counterexample; `unknown` = the solver could not decide, recorded as not-checkable rather than quietly as a pass.

formal_status.description: Written mechanically by spec-record. 'verified' = bounded ✓ (≤max_steps). 'verified-inductive' = proven via inductive invariant (unbounded). 'verified-in-scope' = Alloy found no counterexample within the declared finite scope — bounded by structure, not by steps. 'verified-smt' = an SMT solver proved the negation unsatisfiable, valid modulo the encoding. 'not-checkable' = the chosen backend returned no verdict (SMT 'unknown'); an absent answer, never a pass.

extraction.description: Where this item came from when it was read out of existing code. Makes the confirm pass jump-to-site instead of guess-what-I-meant, and lets the extraction audit tell a specified site from an unexamined one.

fingerprint.description: The extraction_triage[] site this item was read from, when it came from exactly one.

confidence.description: low = the code was ambiguous and a human guessed. Worth revisiting before approval; the readback surfaces it.

inferred_by.description: 'agent' | 'human' | 'agent+confirmed'. A confirmed inference is not the same claim as an unreviewed one.

name.description: Symbolic name used in code, e.g. MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS.

paired_invariant.description: The invariant bounding this constant from the OTHER side. Reachability is one-sided: a witness can show a threshold CAN fire, never that it cannot fire early. With MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS = 5, changing the guard to `>= 1` leaves every invariant holding, the witness still found (in one step), and lint clean — nothing in the chain notices. The paired invariant is what makes the threshold two-sided, e.g. `failedAttempts.get(u) < MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS implies not(isLocked(u))`.

extraction.description: Where this item came from when it was read out of existing code. Makes the confirm pass jump-to-site instead of guess-what-I-meant, and lets the extraction audit tell a specified site from an unexamined one.

fingerprint.description: The extraction_triage[] site this item was read from, when it came from exactly one.

confidence.description: low = the code was ambiguous and a human guessed. Worth revisiting before approval; the readback surfaces it.

inferred_by.description: 'agent' | 'human' | 'agent+confirmed'. A confirmed inference is not the same claim as an unreviewed one.

decisions.description: ADRs. kind='architecture' entries pair with the architecture section to record WHY non-obvious choices were made.

affects.description: IDs this decision governs (REQ-NNN, INV-NNN, CON-NNN, or <area>.<ID> across areas). When the decision changes, this is the blast radius — the list spec-diff reads to say which obligations a reversal puts back in play. spec-lint FAILs a dangling reference.

state_machines.description: Explicit state machines for stateful entities. Optional but valuable: spec-lint validates structural completeness (unreachable states, dangling non-terminal states, transitions referencing undeclared states, Quint mutations not listed as transitions) without needing Apalache. /spec-readback renders the diagram from this section. Each entry corresponds to one entity from concepts.entities[] that has states[].

entity.description: Entity name. Must match a concepts.entities[].name.

quint_var.description: Quint var that holds this state in the sidecar (used by spec-lint to cross-check).

quint_type.description: Quint variant type defining the state values.

initial_state.description: The state the entity is in after `init`. Must appear in states[].

name.description: State name; matches a variant constructor in quint_type.

terminal.description: No outgoing transitions expected. Lint warns if a terminal state has any.

lifecycle_actions.description: Quint actions that mutate quint_var but aren't state transitions on an existing instance — creation, destruction, garbage collection. Suppresses the 'sidecar action mutates quint_var but isn't listed as a transition' warning for these. Example: login creates a Session in initial_state, so it goes here, not in transitions[].

from.description: Origin state (must be in states[]) or '*' meaning 'from any non-terminal state'.

trigger.description: Action or event name; usually matches a Quint action.

actor.description: Who or what initiates the transition: User, Admin, System, etc.

guard.description: Plain-language precondition. The Quint action encodes the formal version.

quint_action.description: Name of the Quint action that realizes this transition. spec-lint checks the sidecar mutation of quint_var matches the transitions listed here.

architecture.description: Per-area architecture (Layer 0-6 except diagrams). Sparse: only declares overrides from project defaults in .spec/project.json. inherits_project=true (default) merges; false makes this fully standalone.

implements.description: Quint action names this component implements.

architecture_file.description: Optional sidecar specs/<area>/components/<name>.json with a fuller per-component architecture.

module_layout.description: Path templates. Variables: {area}, {component}, {ext}. Paths relative to code_root resolved from .spec/project.json.

cross_cutting.description: logging, metrics, tracing, auth, feature_flags. Each is a string or object.

quint_file.description: Sidecar path, e.g. 'auth.qnt' (relative to this JSON). The Quint module is the source of truth for the formal spec; module name and imports are read from it directly via tools/quint_ir.py — never mirrored here.

probe_domains.description: Finite domain each action PARAMETER TYPE is drawn from in the generated stepP, as a Quint set expression: {"UserId": "Set(\"alice\", \"bob\")"}. Keyed by type rather than by parameter name because types are stable while parameter names vary per action. Required by tools/spec-probes.py and deliberately not inferred: how much of the state space the probes explore is a scope decision — too small and a probe cannot fire, too large and every check pays for it — so it is stated in the spec rather than guessed by a generator.

probes_file.description: Generated probe module, e.g. 'auth.probes.qnt' (relative to this JSON). Contains the ghost-instrumented step wrapper and the path-constrained witness probes. Regenerated by /spec-check; never hand-edited.

alloy_file.description: OPTIONAL structural sidecar, e.g. 'user-permission.als' (relative to this JSON). Hand-written Alloy holding the relational/structural checks for this area — typically a contract. Behavior stays in the Quint sidecar; Alloy answers structure-shaped questions (cardinality, referential integrity, ownership) without paying the temporal product cost. Only invariants marked `proof: "structural"` are routed here.

conformance.description: Model-based conformance testing config: how witness traces are replayed against real code. /spec-code-generate generates the adapter and harness; /spec-code-verify runs the command and treats a requirement as verified only when its witness trace replays green.

adapter.description: Path (relative to code root) of the adapter mapping Quint actions to code API calls and Quint vars to observable code state.

harness.description: Path (relative to tests root) of the trace-replay harness that loads ITF files and drives the adapter.

command.description: Shell command that replays all traces, e.g. 'pnpm test conformance'. Run from the code repo root by /spec-code-verify.

pbt_command.description: OPTIONAL stateful property-based testing command. Apalache returns the SHORTEST counterexample, so replay is a handful of traces and a handful of steps per area, each requirement exercised once. The adapter already exposes one method per action, one getter per var and a reset() — which is exactly a stateful-PBT interface, so the same adapter drives thousands of randomized sequences for the price of wiring. Complements replay, never replaces it: replay checks the model's own traces, PBT explores beyond them. The zero-new-code option is quint's own simulator: `quint run --mbt --n-traces=1000 --out-itf=traces/pbt/out.itf.json <area>.qnt` writes out<N>.itf.json traces carrying mbt::actionTaken and mbt::nondetPicks — the same action-plus-arguments the probe module's _last* ghosts carry, so the existing adapter consumes them unchanged (itf_tools.action_params reads both conventions).

traces_dir.description: Where witness traces live, relative to specs/. Default: '<area>/traces'.

differential.description: DIFFERENTIAL conformance, available only to brownfield: the existing implementation is an oracle that answers any question you ask it, and until you ask, extraction fidelity is asserted by a human rather than measured. The comparator instantiates the SAME adapter twice — once over the original, once over the regenerated implementation — drives both through identical sequences, and diffs boundary.observable_state after every step. Each divergence is either a missing spec element (the extraction gap you were hunting) or an intentional difference (record it as a decision).

parallel_path.description: Where /spec-code-generate --parallel writes the regenerated implementation. NEVER the original's path: the oracle has to survive the experiment.

command.description: Shell command running the comparator. Exit 0 = no sequence distinguished the two.

sequences.description: How many randomized sequences the comparator should run. Reported with the verdict, because 'equivalent' means 'no counterexample in N', never 'equivalent'.

traceability.description: Maps each requirement/invariant to its Quint construct, the component implementing it, and the code/test locations. Filled in by /spec-code-generate.

source.description: Where the question came from: matrix, matrix-orphan, red-team:critical, red-team:important, counterexample, elicitation, …

matrix_triage.description: COMMITTED triage decisions for uncovered state×event cells. The matrix CSV under specs/<area>/gen/ is gitignored scratch — decisions recorded only there would vanish on a fresh clone and the --strict CI gate would fail. This section is the durable home; spec-matrix reads it when regenerating and the CSV merely mirrors it.

verdict.description: GAP: a real hole, tracked by a question. IMPOSSIBLE: the cell cannot occur (a guard forbids it). NO-OP: the event CAN occur here and deliberately changes nothing — the third answer a closed specification needs, and the one most often left implicit; name the requirement that decided it in `reason`. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary, and must cite the scope.excluded[] entry that covers it.

reason.description: Why: the impossibility argument, the covering artifact, or (for GAP) the unanswered question.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item that covers this cell. Without it, 'out of scope' is an assertion; with it, it is a reference to a boundary someone reviewed.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

screens.description: Optional on any area. Each screen is a top-level navigable view. Declaring screens[] + navigation[] makes the area an interactive surface: navigation lint, navigation-graph readback, and component codegen activate.

components.description: Names from ui_components[] that appear on this screen.

states.description: Visible states: idle, loading, error, etc.

visible_when.description: Plain-language condition or Quint predicate name.

navigation.description: Allowed transitions between screens (areas with screens). Required when screens[] is declared.

trigger.description: Plain-language user action: 'click "Sign in"', 'submit valid credentials'.

guard.description: Optional precondition referencing a Quint val or another area's state.

generated_from.description: The spec version this area's CODE was generated against, stamped mechanically by `spec-record stamp <area> --generated` at the end of /spec-code-generate. verification_log records that a spec and a code commit were once checked together; this records what the code was BUILT TO, which is a different fact and the one that decides whether regenerating is safe. Absent on any area generated before this block existed, and on every hand-written one — absent means unknown, never means current.

spec_sha.description: git HEAD of the SPEC repo at generation. Locates the exact spec text; moves on every commit, including ones that changed nothing this code depends on.

spec_content_sha.description: itf_tools compute_spec_sha of the area at generation — a hash of the CLAIMS (EARS fields, modality, invariant statements, constraint values, entity states, scope), not of the file. This is the one worth comparing: it moves when the spec's meaning moves and stays put through bookkeeping churn, so `generated-from-stale` fires on a real divergence rather than on a re-run of the checker.

code_sha.description: git HEAD of the CODE repo immediately after generation — the commit the generated code landed in.

code_repo.description: Logical repo name from project.json repos, for the multi-repo case.

extracted_from.description: The code version this area's spec was READ OUT OF, stamped mechanically by `spec-record stamp <area> --extracted` after a brownfield extraction or a re-extraction. Its whole purpose is to give re-extraction a commit range: with it, `spec-record changed <area>` shows WHAT changed since the spec was read; without it, re-extraction can only report which fingerprints are new, never what moved or when. Fingerprints stay the identity mechanism — they survive reformatting and rebases, which a sha does not. This adds the narrative, it does not replace them.

code_sha.description: git HEAD of the code repo when the spec was read from it.

code_path.description: Subtree the extraction read, relative to the code repo root. Narrows the diff to what the spec actually claims to describe.

conformance.description: Trace-replay results from this run (see conformance section).

check_results.description: Latest Apalache results. Overwritten by /spec-check each run.

max_steps.description: Apalache step bound used for the bounded checks in this run. Drives honest '✓ (≤N steps)' rendering — a bounded ✓ is only valid up to this depth.

extraction.description: Code→spec coverage stats from the last tools/spec-extract-audit.py run. The third completeness axis, and the only one that measures the specification against the implementation rather than the other way round.

simulation.description: Result of the last ADVISORY simulator pre-gate (`quint run`, spec-record check step 0). Deliberately kept apart from `checks`: the simulator's '[ok] No violation found' means 'not in the executions I explored', which is not a verdict, so nothing here ever becomes a formal_status and the readback must never render it as a ✓. What it is for: a shallow bug reported in seconds instead of after the model-checking run, and a witness the random search never reaches flagged before Apalache is asked to find it.

backend.description: Evaluator used. Absent when the installed quint predates `quint run --backend` and its own default was used.

max_samples.description: Executions explored. The denominator every count below is honest against.

seed.description: Present only when the run was seeded. Without it the exploration differs run to run, which is the point on a pre-gate but means a finding here is not reproducible by re-running.

result.description: 'ok' is NOT 'verified' — it is 'no violation in max_samples random executions'. Only `checks` carries verdicts.

witnesses.description: Per-probe result of `quint run --witnesses`: in how many explored traces the witness predicate held. 0 of N is the vacuity red flag found cheap — a strong hint the behavior is unreachable, and only a hint, because the simulator is incomplete and the model checker still decides.

differential.description: Result of the last differential run: the original implementation and the regenerated one, driven through the same sequences.

sequences.description: How many were actually run. A verdict without this number claims more than it checked.

outcomes.description: External×outcome coverage stats from the last spec-matrix --outcomes run. The failure-behavior twin of `matrix`: same shape, same purpose — make the completeness of the unhappy paths visible in the readback instead of leaving it to memory.

gaps.description: Q-NNN ids of open GAP cells, if any were filed.

matrix.description: State×event coverage stats from the last spec-matrix run (written by spec-matrix --record). Surfaces completeness in readbacks — the gitignored gen/ CSV is the working file, these counts are the reviewable summary.

gaps.description: Q-NNN ids of open GAP cells, if any were filed.

id.description: INV-NNN or PROP-NNN. Witness results live in requirements[].witness, not here.

over.description: Which module produced this result — echoed from the invariant's `over`. A verdict from the probe module was checked against initP/stepP rather than the sidecar's own init/step, and a reader comparing two ✓ marks should be able to see that.

proof.description: Echo of the invariant's proof mode for this check. 'inductive' verified results are unbounded proofs; 'bounded' are valid only to check_results.max_steps; 'structural' results come from the Alloy backend and are valid only within this entry's `scope`.

backend.description: Which validator produced this result. 'alloy' entries are scope-bounded, not step-bounded — their honesty suffix comes from `scope`, not check_results.max_steps. 'tlc' entries come from the temporal path (properties[], `quint verify --temporal`): explicit-state, so they are bounded by the model's own finite state space rather than by check_results.max_steps, and they carry no `trace` because --out-itf is Apalache-only.

alloy_command.description: For backend 'alloy': the .als check command that was run.

scope.description: For backend 'alloy': the finite scope the verdict is valid within, echoed from the run's receipt.json (e.g. '3 Account, 3 User'). A ✓ outside this scope was never checked.

solver.description: For backend 'alloy': the SAT solver id used (pinned via .spec/project.json alloy.solver). Recorded because a scope-bounded ✓ is only reproducible against a named solver.

instance.description: For backend 'alloy': repo-relative path of the counterexample instance XML. Written under specs/<area>/gen/ — GITIGNORED and regenerable, because Alloy picks one instance out of many and its choice is not stable across solver/tool versions. The verdict is committed; the instance is not.

batched.description: This verdict came from the batched `quint verify --invariants` run that checked every bounded invariant at once. Same check, same bound, one Apalache start for all of them — recorded because a batched ✓ and a per-id ✓ should not be indistinguishable when reading a ledger back.

note.description: Mechanical note about HOW the result was obtained, never about what it means. Written for results whose usual evidence is absent by construction — e.g. a temporal counterexample found by TLC, which produces no ITF trace.

trace.description: Counterexample ITF path relative to specs/, if any.

counterexample.description: NL explanation of the counterexample (nl_explanation). The raw trace lives in the file at `trace`, not inline.
